audit.why: TRICKY at 7.5/10 is right for a 53.67% win rate: Heimerdinger owns levels 2-6 behind the nest, Yasuo owns the crit-item window, and Yasuo's carry threat of 9/10 is the reason the lane still feels dangerous when won.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart gave Levels 2, 3, 4-5 and 6 to Yasuo or Skill while every piece of prose on the page — whys[1..4], spikes[0..2], early and mid — describes those exact stages as Heimerdinger takeovers ('it flips hard', 'his dash-in suicidal', 'this is your takeover'). The packet levelChart also lists Heimerdinger for all four rows.
audit.why: Prose, packet and the two chart layers must agree, otherwise the page tells a paying user he loses the exact stage the same page tells him to fight in.
audit.corrected: Levels 2, 3, 4-5 and 6 -> Heimerdinger, ratings raised to 7/10, with the whys rewritten to state the mechanic instead of a generic reminder. First item and 2+ items stay Yasuo.

audit.whatIsWrong: Wind Wall is described only as blocking 'turret beams + your Q', and no cooldown is ever given. In fact every damaging tool Heimerdinger owns is a projectile — H-28G turret beams, Hextech Micro-Rockets (W) and the CH-3X grenade (E) — so a 4-second wall blanks his whole kit, and it is on 25/23/21/19/17s. Steel Tempest's 2-stack knockup is never named as the enabler for Last Breath either.
audit.why: Heimerdinger's kit flags every ability as projectile; Yasuo's W flag is blocksProjectiles with a 4s duration and a 25s rank-1 cooldown. The 21s of downtime after a baited wall is the concrete engage window the page was gesturing at without numbers. Last Breath (70/50/30s) requires an Airborne target, and the only source Yasuo has alone is Steel Tempest at 2 stacks of Gathering Storm.
audit.corrected: State that Wind Wall eats beams, rockets and the grenade alike, that it is 4s up and 25s down at rank 1, and that CH-3X should be held for the Steel Tempest knockup rather than spent on poke.

audit.whatIsWrong: The most punishable cooldown in the lane was named but never quantified.
audit.why: Wind Wall at rank 1 is 25s on a 4s duration — 21 seconds where nothing you throw is blocked. CH-3X's flat 11s cooldown is the matching restraint on your side.
audit.corrected: Numbers added to dosFull[0].d and report[5].t.

audit.whatIsWrong: dontsFull[1].d ('Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.') did not describe the mistake in its own title.
audit.why: The real error is spending CH-3X before the Steel Tempest knockup lands.
audit.corrected: Rewritten to name Steel Tempest's 2-stack knockup as the thing you save the grenade for.

edits.after: Your second H-28G and its slowing beam wall a zone his dash only feeds into — Wind Wall is down 25s at rank 1.

edits.after: Three turret charges down: any Sweeping Blade dash-in eats stacked beam DPS before he ever reaches you.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Wind Wall's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: CH-3X center-stun plus a full nest makes his dash-in suicidal — stunned by the grenade and melted by three turrets at once.

edits.before: Upgraded E or W deletes his all-in — choose per fight. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Yasuo's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: UPGRADE!!! widens CH-3X so it catches his dash and the nest finishes him through flow shield. Last Breath still needs a knockup first.

edits.before: Track Yasuo's Wind Wall: Blocks turret beams + your Q. Bait it. When it is down — E-stun + turret him.
edits.after: Wind Wall blocks every projectile you own — beams, W rockets, CH-3X. It lasts 4s and is down 25s at rank 1.

edits.before: Blocks turret beams + your Q. Bait it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Bait the 4s wall with one rocket, then commit — it is down 25s at rank 1.

edits.after: Steel Tempest at 2 stacks knocks up — hold CH-3X for that, not for poke.

notes: Four chart rows (Levels 2, 3, 4-5, 6) were flipped to Heimerdinger as one atomic group with matched full/content pairs and ratings; First item and 2+ items were left with Yasuo, which matches the packet, the win rate and the existing late-game prose. I did not write the commonly-cited claim that Sweeping Blade can dash through Heimerdinger's turrets — Riot's text only says 'target enemy' and the kit file cannot confirm whether deployed turrets are valid dash targets; logged in unverified.
